look_here_first: Look BELOW EACH HEAD for a second, obvious ARMOR COLLAR: a ring of spiny-margined leaflike bracts about as long as the 30–50 mm involucre. Those are separate SUBTENDING BRACTS, not the individual phyllaries of the involucre. Leaves often bear stout main marginal spines (5–30 mm, variable by variety) and cauline leaf bases may be auriculate-clasping. Color varies white/yellow/pink/purple—yellow thistle is not necessarily yellow. Compared with C. vulgare check the UPPER LEAF BLADE for bristle-spines, not just rough marginal prickles.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Ring of spiny-margined leaflike bracts RIGHT BENEATH EACH INDIVIDUAL head, about involucre length: strongest separator.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Involucre (green cup beneath florets) ~30–50 mm tall, much larger than C. texanum's ~12–20 mm.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Primary leaf-edge spines may be 5–30 mm; C. horridulum has marked infraspecific variation.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Biennial or sometimes persistent perennial/root-sprouting habit; do not insist annual-only.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: White/yellow to pink/purple/red heads can occur; color does NOT separate from native Texas thistle.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: Do not substitute marginal thorns for C. vulgare's short leaf-surface spines.
